body:
If v(t)=3t², the acceleration at t=2 s is

A. 3 m/s²
B. 6 m/s²
C. 12 m/s²
D. 24 m/s²

Choices:
A. 3 m/s²
B. 6 m/s²
C. 12 m/s²
D. 24 m/s²

The displacement from t=0 to T for v(t)=kt is

A. kT
B. kT²
C. kT²/2
D. k/T

Choices:
A. kT
B. kT²
C. kT²/2
D. k/T

A force F(x)=ax acts in one dimension. The work from 0 to L is

A. aL
B. aL²
C. aL²/2
D. a/L

Choices:
A. aL
B. aL²
C. aL²/2
D. a/L

A particle moves in one dimension under a conservative force with potential energy U(x). The force on the particle is given by which of the following?

A. dU/dx
B. -dU/dx
C. -U/x
D. +d^2U/dx^2

Choices:
A. dU/dx
B. -dU/dx
C. -U/x
D. +d^2U/dx^2

A power law P(t)=ct² delivers energy from 0 to T equal to

A. cT²
B. cT³/2
C. cT³/3
D. 2cT

Choices:
A. cT²
B. cT³/2
C. cT³/3
D. 2cT

At a stable equilibrium x₀, U(x) has

A. a local minimum
B. a local maximum
C. an infinite slope
D. no derivative

Choices:
A. a local minimum
B. a local maximum
C. an infinite slope
D. no derivative

Torque from potential energy U(θ), for a system whose potential energy depends only on the angle θ, is

A. dU/dθ
B. -dU/dθ
C. -U/θ
D. +d²U/dθ²

Choices:
A. dU/dθ
B. -dU/dθ
C. -U/θ
D. +d²U/dθ²

If x(t)=At³-Bt, velocity is

A. 3At²-B
B. At²-B
C. 3At-B
D. A t³

Choices:
A. 3At²-B
B. At²-B
C. 3At-B
D. A t³

A force F(x)=F₀e^{-x/L} acts along the direction of displacement, with L a positive constant. The work done as the object moves from x=0 to x→∞ is

A. F₀/L
B. F₀L
C. zero
D. infinite

Choices:
A. F₀/L
B. F₀L
C. zero
D. infinite

For τ(t)=τ₀t acting on constant I, change in angular speed from 0 to T is

A. τ₀T/I
B. τ₀T²/(2I)
C. Iτ₀T²
D. τ₀T²/I

Choices:
A. τ₀T/I
B. τ₀T²/(2I)
C. Iτ₀T²
D. τ₀T²/I

For a physical pendulum undergoing small-angle oscillation, omega^2 equals which of the following, where d is the distance from the pivot to the center of mass and I is the moment of inertia about the pivot?

A. mgd/I
B. I/mgd
C. g/I
D. mgI/d

Choices:
A. mgd/I
B. I/mgd
C. g/I
D. mgI/d

For x(t)=Ct⁴, acceleration is

A. 4Ct³
B. 12Ct²
C. 24Ct
D. Ct²

Choices:
A. 4Ct³
B. 12Ct²
C. 24Ct
D. Ct²

The signed area under a velocity-versus-time graph equals

A. acceleration
B. displacement
C. distance traveled
D. change in velocity

Choices:
A. acceleration
B. displacement
C. distance traveled
D. change in velocity

A block slides down a frictionless incline at angle θ. The normal force on the block is

A. mg
B. mg sinθ
C. mg cosθ
D. 0

Choices:
A. mg
B. mg sinθ
C. mg cosθ
D. 0

For U(x)=(1/2)kx² with k>0, x=0 is stable because

A. U has a local minimum
B. U has a local maximum
C. force is constant
D. energy is negative

Choices:
A. U has a local minimum
B. U has a local maximum
C. force is constant
D. energy is negative

For m dv/dt=-bv, the characteristic decay time is

A. b/m
B. m/b
C. m/(2b)
D. (m/b) ln 2

Choices:
A. b/m
B. m/b
C. m/(2b)
D. (m/b) ln 2

A particle in uniform circular motion has

A. zero acceleration
B. constant velocity vector
C. inward acceleration v²/r
D. outward net force

Choices:
A. zero acceleration
B. constant velocity vector
C. inward acceleration v²/r
D. outward net force

The work done from x=a to x=b by F(x) is

A. ∫ₐᵇF(x)dx
B. F(b)(b-a)
C. (1/2)[F(a)+F(b)](b-a) always
D. ∫F(t)dt

Choices:
A. ∫ₐᵇF(x)dx
B. F(b)(b-a)
C. (1/2)[F(a)+F(b)](b-a) always
D. ∫F(t)dt

For U(x)=Ax³, the force is

A. 3Ax²
B. -3Ax²
C. -Ax²
D. -(A/3)x²

Choices:
A. 3Ax²
B. -3Ax²
C. -Ax²
D. -(A/3)x²

At a one-dimensional classical turning point with total energy E,

A. U=0 always
B. U=E and speed is zero
C. force must be zero
D. kinetic energy is maximum

Choices:
A. U=0 always
B. U=E and speed is zero
C. force must be zero
D. kinetic energy is maximum

A force F acts on a particle with velocity v. Instantaneous power is

A. F·v
B. F×v
C. Fv regardless of direction
D. F·a

Choices:
A. F·v
B. F×v
C. Fv regardless of direction
D. F·a

For constant mass m and v(t), net force equals

A. mv/t
B. m dv/dt
C. v dm/dt only
D. (1/2)m dv/dt

Choices:
A. mv/t
B. m dv/dt
C. v dm/dt only
D. (1/2)m dv/dt

In an isolated perfectly inelastic collision,

A. momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
B. momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not
C. kinetic energy is conserved but momentum is not
D. neither total energy nor momentum is conserved

Choices:
A. momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
B. momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not
C. kinetic energy is conserved but momentum is not
D. neither total energy nor momentum is conserved

For circular orbits about the same mass, doubling radius multiplies period by

A. sqrt2
B. 2
C. 2sqrt2
D. 4

Choices:
A. sqrt2
B. 2
C. 2sqrt2
D. 4
